lever: One appended prompt rule: when a change makes a function accept new inputs (looser matching, a new option, a new argument type), the check must also assert what the function returns for those inputs: the same type, and when the caller passes a set of allowed values, one of them exactly as declared rather than the raw input.
why: Five box runs (v7, v7c, b1024, v0-think and v13 itself) implemented the looser match and returned the typed text; their own checks asserted only acceptance. Measured on the issue's own example (edge_sweep in the ground-truth JSON): each of the five patches returns a value outside the declared choices for 3 of 4 newly accepted inputs, so a one-line membership assert fails on all five and passes on gold. The five submitted with 60-170 s left. 0 malformed calls in all seven runs (the old EDIT_TOOL_FAILURE label no longer applies).
baseline: never solved: p4 (v5h2), p4_v7, p4_v7c, p4_v7d, p4_b1024 (v12-b1024), p4_v0t2 (v0-think), p4_v13 (v13); 0 of 12 Kaggle L4 runs
applies_outside_the_42: fastapi_9425 (contested: a response that must keep returning no body after the change); any normalising option such as case-insensitive enum or CLI-choice matching on hidden repos
risk: Built on v13 (one first-reply plain-text tool call seen on the v13 box run; earlier runs had 10 such replies that recovered); the added rule has no code fence and no tool-call-like syntax. A return-value assert costs one more check call.
